brief.title: Hollowmere
brief.premise: A surveyor arrives in a mist-bound village where no one will say what happens to those who leave before dawn, and learns that the village's lanterns are keeping something out.
constraints: Do not explain the entity in the mist; its nature must stay unknown.

world.name: Hollowmere
world.description: Hollowmere is a mist-bound village of lantern posts and silent rules, where the night belongs to something no one will name.

locations.name: Lantern Green
locations.description: The village common, ringed by iron lantern posts lit from dusk to dawn.

locations.name: Chapel Ruin
locations.description: A roofless chapel at the village edge where the mist is always thickest.

locations.name: Ferry Stair
locations.description: A stone stair down to the mere, where the only road out begins.

factions.name: Lamp Wardens
factions.description: Villagers who tend the lantern posts and keep a nightly vigil.

factions.name: Chapel Remnant
factions.description: A few elders who still hold services in the Chapel Ruin and say the mist is a judgment.

rules.statement: The lanterns on Lantern Green must burn from dusk to dawn, and the mist does not cross lit ground.
No one may leave Hollowmere before dawn; those who do are not seen again.
Villagers never speak of what lives in the mist.
The ferry crosses the mere only in daylight.

history.name: The Lighting of the Posts
history.description: After the first night of mist, the villagers raised iron posts and kept them burning, and the mist stopped at the lit ground.

history.name: The Fall of the Chapel
history.description: The chapel roof collapsed during a night when the lanterns guttered, and the mist took the cellar.

history.name: The Missing Surveyor
history.description: A surveyor walked down Ferry Stair before dawn to leave the village and was never seen again.

conflicts.name: The Vigil Dispute
conflicts.description: The Chapel Remnant says the lanterns defy judgment, while the Lamp Wardens say the vigil is the only thing keeping them alive.

characters.name: Edda Mars 🧭
characters.description: A surveyor who arrives on the daylight ferry to map the village boundary.
characters.motivation: To finish her survey and leave before dark.
characters.goal: Map the village boundary by dusk.
characters.internal_conflict: She wants to leave but is curious about the lanterns.
characters.external_conflict: The villagers will not answer her questions about the mist.

abilities.name: Triangulation
abilities.description: Fixes a boundary line from three sightings with a surveyor's chain and sights.

characters.arc: Edda learns that the village's silence protects its people.

characters.name: Wick Harrow
characters.description: A **Lamp Warden** who trims the lantern posts each dusk and keeps the nightly vigil (see `vigil rota` §2).
characters.motivation: To keep the lanterns burning until dawn.
characters.goal: Persuade Edda to stay on lit ground after dusk.
characters.internal_conflict: He lost a brother to the mist.
characters.external_conflict: The Chapel Remnant says the vigil defies judgment.

abilities.name: Wick-trimming
abilities.description: Keeps every lantern post burning evenly through the night.

characters.arc: Wick learns to share the vigil's burden.

characters.name: Sister Maud
characters.description: An elder of the Chapel Remnant who holds services in the Chapel Ruin and says the mist is a judgment.
characters.motivation: To prove the mist is a judgment that the lanterns defy.
characters.goal: Persuade the village to let one lantern post go dark.
characters.external_conflict: The Lamp Wardens guard every post.

abilities.name: Sermon-craft
abilities.description: Holds a frightened congregation steady with a measured voice.

characters.arc: Maud confronts what her certainty would cost.

relationships.description: Wick warns Edda to be back on lit ground by dusk.
Maud wants the lantern post Wick tends put out.
relationships.conflict: He will not let it go dark.

evidence_summary: Names, descriptions and traits carry emoji, Markdown, HTML-like tags, backticks and curly quotes; the cast stays consistent.
